headline_marked: Tensions rise as [[Iran attacks US naval drone]] in Strait of Hormuz
headline: Tensions rise as Iran attacks US naval drone in Strait of Hormuz
summary: The attack comes amid a cycle of strikes between Tehran and Washington, with Iran warning of 'faster, heavier, and more painful' responses to aggression.
details: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they attacked a US military unmanned surface vessel attempting to enter the protected area of the Strait of Hormuz.
The incident occurred hours after Tehran and Washington traded strikes, marking a new escalation in their ongoing six-month conflict.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned that any further aggression against Iran would be met with a response that is 'faster, heavier, and more painful'.
Meanwhile, US Central Command reported that as of September 6, it has redirected 92 commercial vessels and disabled three others to enforce a blockade.
In a separate escalation, Israel carried out strikes in south Lebanon that killed four people and injured 20 more, following drone attacks by Hezbollah.
Iranian authorities have also arrested several individuals after a video emerged showing them waving the flag of the outlawed People's Mujahedin Organisation of Iran (MEK).
Diplomatic efforts continue as Turkish and Iranian foreign ministers discussed regional developments and ongoing negotiations with the US via telephone.
caption:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards have attacked a US naval drone in the Strait of Hormuz as tensions between Tehran and Washington reach a boiling point.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they attacked a US military unmanned surface vessel attempting to enter the protected area of the Strait of Hormuz.

The incident occurred hours after Tehran and Washington traded strikes, marking a new escalation in their ongoing six-month conflict.

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned that any further aggression against Iran would be met with a response that is 'faster, heavier, and more painful'.

Meanwhile, US Central Command reported that as of September 6, it has redirected 92 commercial vessels and disabled three others to enforce a blockade.

In a separate escalation, Israel carried out strikes in south Lebanon that killed four people and injured 20 more, following drone attacks by Hezbollah.

Iranian authorities have also arrested several individuals after a video emerged showing them waving the flag of the outlawed People's Mujahedin Organisation of Iran (MEK).

Diplomatic efforts continue as Turkish and Iranian foreign ministers discussed regional developments and ongoing negotiations with the US via telephone.

headline_marked: Up to 50 students feared trapped as [[Delhi hostel building collapses]]
headline: Up to 50 students feared trapped as Delhi hostel building collapses
summary: At least three people have died and several others are injured after a five-storey boys' PG hostel in South-West Delhi collapsed yesterday afternoon.
details: A five-storey boys' PG hostel, known as 'Hostel Daze', collapsed in South-West Delhi yesterday afternoon. Preliminary inquiries suggest around 40-50 students were inside the building at the time of the incident.
Rescue operations are being carried out on a 'war footing' by teams from the NDRF, Delhi Fire Services, Delhi Police, and other emergency agencies.
Hospital authorities report that at least three people have died and two others are in critical condition. Nine students have already been rescued from the rubble and admitted to nearby hospitals.
An eyewitness reported that an adjacent building also collapsed during the incident, trapping students in their rooms under the debris.
The South Campus Police Station received a PCR call regarding the collapse at approximately 1:34 pm yesterday.
caption:
Up to 50 students feared trapped after a five-storey hostel building collapses in Delhi.

A five-storey boys' PG hostel, known as 'Hostel Daze', collapsed in South-West Delhi yesterday afternoon. Preliminary inquiries suggest around 40-50 students were inside the building at the time of the incident.

Rescue operations are being carried out on a 'war footing' by teams from the NDRF, Delhi Fire Services, Delhi Police, and other emergency agencies.

Hospital authorities report that at least three people have died and two others are in critical condition. Nine students have already been rescued from the rubble and admitted to nearby hospitals.

An eyewitness reported that an adjacent building also collapsed during the incident, trapping students in their rooms under the debris.

The South Campus Police Station received a PCR call regarding the collapse at approximately 1:34 pm yesterday.
